- South Asia: Top UN court finds Myanmar committed state-sponsored genocide against Muslim Rohingya.
- India: Trump pushes Iran war decision to 2027, says he'll 'see what happens' after Jan 1.

- Jamaica Gleaner, 17 hours ago: From war zone to white coat - Ukraine escapee graduates as doctor after mother’s 16-hour work shifts helped finance his education.
WESTERN BUREAU: Four years ago, Joel Tulloch was fleeing Russian bombs in war-torn Ukraine, uncertain whether he would ever complete the medical training he had started there. On Sunday, inside the Marjorie Myers Hall at Shortwood Teachers’ College in St Andrew, Tulloch’s ambitious endeavour became a reality as he collected his medical degree, having completed his studies at the Caribbean School of Medical Sciences, Jamaica (CSMSJ).

Property owners sitting on derelict buildings in Montego Bay, St James, are being urged to invest in their properties or sell them, as business and civic leaders push to transform the western city into what they envision as the Caribbean’s next capital. In a blunt warning, Jason Russell, president of the Montego Bay Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said prime properties in high-visibility tourism and entertainment areas could no longer be allowed to remain idle while the country pursues economic growth.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Top UN court finds Myanmar committed state-sponsored genocide against Muslim Rohingya.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 10 hours ago: Top UN court finds Myanmar committed state-sponsored genocide against Muslim Rohingya.
The highest United Nations court ruled on Thursday that thousands of killings and widespread sexual violence by Myanmar’s security forces against the Rohingya Muslim minority population in 2017 amounted to state-sponsored genocide. The decision, seven years after the case was filed by predominantly Muslim Gambia, marked only the fourth time since the Nazi Holocaust that an international court ruled that the legal threshold to prove genocide had been met. It was the first time the court held a state responsible for genocide.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 16 hours ago: CDF Munir briefed on ongoing operations during Balochistan visit: ISPR.
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir was briefed on counterterrorism operations during a visit to Turbat, Balochistan, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a press release on Thursday. CDF Munir received a comprehensive briefing on “the prevailing security environment, operational preparedness and successful ongoing operations against externally sponsored terrorism”, ISPR said. He was also informed of progress in ongoing socioeconomic development initiatives in Balochistan.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 13 hours ago: Navy’s combat capabilities significantly enhanced across all operational domains: Admiral Ashraf.
Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS) Admiral Naveed Ashraf on Thursday said the Pakistan Navy has significantly enhanced its combat capabilities across all operational domains. He made the remarks while addressing the graduation parade of the Pakistan Air Force Academy Asghar Khan in Risalpur in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Nowshera district. CNS Admiral Ashraf stated that the Pakistan Navy was making significant headway towards modernising its fleet.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, 4 hours ago: US, China, Russia sign ‘peace declaration’ after historic Trump, Xi, Putin meeting.
China, the United States and Russia issued a “Declaration toward Peace” on Thursday after their leaders held an unprecedented summit, laying out common ambitions to overhaul the UN and keep the International Criminal Court (ICC) in check. The statement, issued after Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China, said they wanted to protect diplomatic immunity for state officials and also boost supply and production of refined petroleum products.
